reviews.review:
the pros:
[list]
[*] fairly solid unlockable system for a 2020s game from a AAA publisher. no online requirement this time, as far as i'm aware
[*] the gameplay is effectively identical to pro skater 1+2, and 1+2's gameplay was of a reasonably high quality
[*] there are two new levels, and they're alright, though they feel a little on the smaller side
[*] my friends and i had fun looking around the levels in photo mode and making soy faces at the scenery
[*] i couldn't tell which art assets were computer-generated, for what that's worth. maybe the scenery for the pinball level? (per other reviews, the use of generative AI was not disclosed before release, which would explain why i wasn't immediately aware of any such content)
[/list]

the cons:
[list]
[*] pro skater 4 is not faithfully remade. two and a half levels (six and a half if you include version exclusives from both original games) have been cut and pro skater 4's mission system has been removed in favor of the arcade-style career that appeared in the first three games. activision and iron galaxy made an intentional design decision, and were upfront about the change. however, i say it was an incorrect move
[*] pro skater 1+2 was a compelling purchase because it finally allowed the two games to be played with a more up-to-date set of skating mechanics based on pro skater 4. pro skater 3+4 reuses the previous game's pseudo-pro skater 4 mechanics verbatim, with no additions of its own. this is not a drawback in itself, but i can't point to anything else that i could call a selling point for 3+4, much less anything that could possibly justify a markup in price compared to the previous game
[*] the character customization system is very robust, if you want to create a normie who wears supreme merch unironically. otherwise, it is weaker than that of the original games
[*] the game claims to be compatible with playstation controllers. this is accurate, insofar as plugging in a playstation controller will make the game do something. that thing is "freak out and become unplayable". steam input is required to make the game treat your controller as an xbox controller, which works as intended
[*] jack black is still not funny, which is why he has a bigger role here than in 1+2
[*] doomguy, who was unlockable in the original pro skater 3, is now a ridiculously overpriced paid DLC
[*] i thought 1+2 had a lousy original soundtrack, but i would rather listen to cherry kola from 1+2 on loop for 72 hours than 100 gecs in 3+4 once
[*] here's a nitpick that really bothered me: there is a one-off character that is identified as eric sparrow. the player would not know this is eric sparrow without being told so, because he neither looks nor sounds anything like eric sparrow. fake eric's dialogue explicitly refers to the player character as the same skater from underground 1 and 2, so this cannot have been an easter egg someone slipped in under the boss's nose. eric's original voice actor is still active in the industry, so activision must have consciously chosen not to hire him. did the dev team honestly think this was a respectful nod to the underground games, or is activision trying to edge us on the prospect of an underground 1+2 remake? i can't tell
[*] bizarre, saccharine presentation that comes off like a marketing department racing to the lowest common denominator in an attempt to make the most wholesome, inoffensive game possible. this game feels like it exists in the same cinematic universe as every TV advertisement for home insurance. for example:
[olist]
[*] anything remotely edgy has been sanitized, to the point where the game goes out of its way to show the player that nobody is hurt in any of the catastrophic car crashes. you could eat off of this game, for how squeaky-clean it is
[*] beating a skater's career unlocks a written message from tony himself. it was probably intended to be inspirational, but it reads like he came up with it with zero notice. you can almost feel the team deciding whether to transcribe his "um"s and "ah"s
[*] the nicest thing activision has to say about bam margera is that they would [i]never[/i] omit such a beloved character from the remake. note: tony pulled rank and forced activision to include bam against their will
[*] the game fanboys really hard for amputee skater felipe nunes. the player has to impress him in two levels, he gets his own cutscenes, and not only does he get a spot in the intro cutscene despite not being playable, but he's the only one with a unique nameplate. if i was in his place, i'd feel like i was being exploited for brownie points
[/olist]
[/list]

this game disappoints me. i was called a shameless slop-guzzling consoomer for having preordered the deluxe edition, and i'm inclined to agree. it doesn't feel like an improvement over the original games on any level except graphical realism. i don't think it's controversial to say the game is obviously an attempt to pander to the nostalgia of gamers who grew up around the turn of the century, but the design philosophy feels like every decision was subject to the final approval of a board of stockholders, marketing consultants and liberal arts graduates. it definitely plays like a pro skater game, but i can't imagine this being anyone's favorite entry in the series; it doesn't do anything to stand out from either the 1+2 remake or the original 3 and 4. i would recommend this remake to people who only own a ps5/switch/xbox series x and have no way of playing the original games, or parents who want to get their children interested in retro gaming.
